text.arabic_uthmani: قَالُوٓا۟ أَوَلَمْ تَكُ تَأْتِيكُمْ رُسُلُكُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ ۖ قَالُوا۟ بَلَىٰ ۚ قَالُوا۟ فَٱدْعُوا۟ ۗ وَمَا دُعَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ

words.gloss_range: reported speech that opens the keepers' cross-examination as a completed tribunal-like utterance
words.root_gloss_range: saying, uttering, declaring, and taking a verbal position; the local Form I perfect selects direct reported speech with accountable quote scope

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: clear proofs that close the opening question
lostness and misdirection as the final verdict-domain

words.prose: {{ar:قَالُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:qālū}}) does not merely report noise in the scene; it opens a quoted cross-examination whose scope runs through the proof phrase. The perfect form makes the future exchange sound like settled record, while the plural ending keeps the keepers present as the compact speaking group. Because this is the first of three saying frames, the reader hears speech become the mechanism of judgment: question, admission, and command all narrow toward {{ar:ضَلَٰلٍ}} ({{tr:ḍalālin}}).

topics.headline: settled opening cross-examination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins as an accountable quoted interrogation, not as neutral scene-setting.
topics.reason: The perfect speech verb governs the full quoted question, and attachment evidence makes the question the quoted complement.

topics.headline: speech as evidentiary channel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees speech functioning as the channel that puts prior notice on record and forces a verbal answer.
topics.reason: The local Form I active speech verb opens direct address, and the following answer confirms its evidentiary function.

topics.headline: three speech turns structure judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the repeated saying frame organize the scene into interrogation, concession, and procedural dismissal.
topics.reason: The ayah contains three matched speech verbs, each introducing a different speech-act role.

words.gloss_range: interrogative-plus-linking particle that resumes the prior plea and turns the negated proposition into rebuke

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: past-negating jussive particle under the question

words.prose: {{ar:أَوَ}} ({{tr:ʾawa}}) fuses question force with discourse linkage. It connects the plea for relief to the proof-question and lets the interrogative scope over the negated clause, so the issue becomes whether non-arrival can still be claimed. In context the question is rebuke: the keepers are not asking for information but forcing the appeal to face its own history.

topics.headline: rebuking question over negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle makes the accused answer a proposition framed as an impossible denial.
topics.reason: The particle opens the quoted question and scopes over the following negated clause.

topics.headline: prior plea linked to proof-test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the plea for relief tied directly to the evidence that invalidates it.
topics.reason: The particle bundle combines interrogative force with a linking element before the proof question.

words.gloss_range: past-negating jussive particle that sets up a denial for reversal by the answer particle

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: answer particle that reverses the negative question

words.prose: {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) carries the denial that the question will overturn. It governs the clipped jussive form after it, making the grammar of non-arrival visible before {{ar:بَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:balā}}) reverses that denial into confession. The particle therefore makes the exchange prosecutorial: the accused are asked whether the very non-arrival claim can survive.

topics.headline: denial built for reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denial is staged only so the answer can overturn it as admission.
topics.reason: The jussive negator governs the following verb, and the later answer particle reverses the negative question.

topics.headline: particle controls clipped verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the denial shaping the following verb form rather than floating as a loose negative word.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the following verb as the complement governed by the negating particle.

words.gloss_range: clipped copular/state frame under negation that treats messenger-arrival as an obtained factual situation
words.root_gloss_range: being, occurring, obtaining, coming to be, and state-holding range; the local apocopated imperfect selects an existential or copular frame rather than independent place, surety, or derivative branches

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: past-negating jussive particle governing this clipped form
arrival reaching the addressees

words.prose: {{ar:تَكُ}} ({{tr:taku}}) turns the coming of messengers into the case that either obtained or did not obtain. Its clipped form under {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) keeps the focus moving quickly toward {{ar:تَأْتِيكُمْ}} ({{tr:taʾtīkum}}), but the copular frame matters: the question is about an established proof-situation, not a bare movement report. The feminine agreement treats the following messenger-arrival as one collective evidentiary event.

topics.headline: arrival framed as obtained fact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the dispute is whether a whole proof-situation stood against them.
topics.reason: The local verb is a copular imperfect under negation, and V4 supports the being or obtaining range for the local form.

topics.headline: feminine singular treats plural as event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees multiple messengers gathered grammatically into one accountable arrival-event.
topics.reason: The feminine singular form anticipates the following broken-plural subject and is also clipped by the negating particle.

topics.headline: speech fixes the fact to be admitted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the keepers' speech aimed at a factual state the inmates must acknowledge.
topics.reason: The local saying frame introduces the question, while this verb frames the reality that the answer concedes.

words.gloss_range: arrival that successfully reaches the accused addressees, with proof-delivery foregrounded before the agents are named
words.root_gloss_range: coming, arriving, reaching, bringing, and coming upon range; the local imperfect with second-person object suffix selects arrival-to-recipient rather than a remote or abstract presence

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: their messengers as delayed subject of the arrival

words.prose: {{ar:تَأْتِيكُمْ}} ({{tr:taʾtīkum}}) makes the addressees the reached party. The question is not whether messengers existed somewhere else, but whether arrival reached these people, and the attached suffix builds that accountability into the verb itself. Its imperfect shape under past negation re-presents the prior arrival vividly, and its position before {{ar:رُسُلُكُم}} ({{tr:rusulukum}}) foregrounds the impact on the recipients before naming the carriers.

topics.headline: arrival reaches the accused
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the warning is charged as delivered to them personally, not merely available elsewhere.
topics.reason: The second-person object suffix is attached to the arrival verb, and attachment evidence identifies it as the reached object or recipient.

topics.headline: messenger arrival as one evidence-event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees prophetic coming treated as proof-delivery rather than movement alone.
topics.reason: The feminine singular agreement fits the following broken-plural subject, and the proof phrase is attached to the arrival.

topics.headline: vivid arrival before agents
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the past warning brought back before the accused before the messengers are named.
topics.reason: The imperfect follows the past-negating particle, and word order places the recipient-impact verb before the subject.

words.gloss_range: their messengers as commissioned proof-bearing subject, plural and possessed by the addressees
words.root_gloss_range: sending, dispatching, commissioning, and communicating a message; the local plural noun selects sent messengers rather than unrelated sending or release branches

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: clear evidences carried with the messengers

words.prose: {{ar:رُسُلُكُم}} ({{tr:rusulukum}}) names the delayed subject of the arrival after the verb has already reached the addressees. The possessive suffix makes the messengers relevant to them, not distant figures, and the plural blocks a single-warning defense by placing multiple or repeated bearers behind the admission. The root carries commissioned sending with communicated charge, so these are proof-bearing envoys tied to {{ar:ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ}} ({{tr:al-bayyināti}}), not mere visitors. The compressed reading tightens the sound without changing subjecthood, possession, or the proof-carrier accusation.

topics.headline: their own proof-bearing messengers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the messengers are grammatically tied to the accused as relevant witnesses against them.
topics.reason: The noun carries a second-person possessive suffix and serves as the explicit subject of the arrival verb.

topics.headline: plural prevents single-warning escape
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the admission backed by a plurality of commissioned warning, not a single ambiguous encounter.
topics.reason: The local noun is plural and is tied to the proof-bearing arrival.

topics.headline: proof-carrier link survives compressed reading
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that variant compression changes sound but not the accusation: commissioned messengers came with clarifying proof.
topics.reason: The cited variant preserves subjecthood and possession, while the local prepositional phrase attaches proof to the arrival.

words.gloss_range: bound preposition attaching the clear proofs as means, accompaniment, or evidentiary payload of the messengers' coming

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the proof noun governed by the preposition

words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) binds the proofs to the arrival. It lets the messengers come with, by means of, and on the evidentiary basis of {{ar:ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ}} ({{tr:al-bayyināti}}), so arrival cannot be separated from proof. Because the question ends on this prepositional phrase, clarity is the final pressure before the one-word admission.

topics.headline: proof attached to coming
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that messenger-arrival is proof-bearing arrival, not a separable visit plus later evidence.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the following proof noun as the prepositional complement attached to the arrival verb.

topics.headline: question ends on clarity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the question land on proof just before the compelled answer.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase occupies the end of the opening question before the answer turn.

words.gloss_range: definite plural clear proofs, publicly recognizable and attached to messenger-arrival as the evidentiary payload
words.root_gloss_range: clarifying, making distinct, separating, manifesting, and clear proof range; the local definite plural noun selects clear evidences rather than unrelated separation branches

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition governing this proof noun
lostness that answers rejected clarity

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ}} ({{tr:al-bayyināti}}) is not an indefinite hint but recognizable clear proofs. The definite plural gives cumulative public clarity, and its government by {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) attaches that clarity to the messengers' arrival. This makes the later lostness sharper: the ayah moves from proof that made things distinct to {{ar:ضَلَٰلٍ}} ({{tr:ḍalālin}}), within the same-surah proof thread (40:22) and against the verification contrast (49:6), so failure happens after clarification, not because warning was obscure.

topics.headline: recognizable plural proofs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the admission concedes public, cumulative clarity rather than private or ambiguous hints.
topics.reason: The local noun is definite and plural, and V4 supports a proof and clarification range for this form.

topics.headline: proof payload governed by preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the proof noun grammatically attached to the messengers' coming as its evidentiary payload.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes this noun the complement of the preceding preposition linked to the arrival.

topics.headline: clarity answered by lostness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same-surah proof thread (40:22) and the verification contrast (49:6) sharpen the final lostness as rejected clarity, not the absence of guidance.
topics.reason: The same ayah names clear proofs before ending with lostness, while the concrete 40:22 and 49:6 references preserve the after-clarification payoff.

words.gloss_range: reported answer-speech that records the inmates' collective concession before the one-word admission
words.root_gloss_range: saying, uttering, declaring, and taking a verbal stance; the local Form I perfect selects direct accountable reply

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the one-word concession carried by this speech verb

words.prose: {{ar:قَالُوا۟}} ({{tr:qālū}}) transfers the speech turn to the accused, and the only content it carries is {{ar:بَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:balā}}). The perfect frames the admission as a completed record, while Form I and the plural ending leave no causative, passive, or individual distance. Speech answers speech here, but the answer confirms the charge rather than contesting it.

topics.headline: collective admission on record
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the inmates' own speech turn become a recorded group concession.
topics.reason: The perfect plural speech verb introduces the single answer particle as its quoted complement.

topics.headline: speech confirms the premise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the accused create evidence against their own plea by answering without defense.
topics.reason: The direct speech frame contains concession rather than explanation or objection.

words.gloss_range: answer particle that reverses the negative question and affirms that the messengers did come

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the consequential command that follows the admission

words.prose: {{ar:بَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:balā}}) is selected because the question was negative. It overturns the denial and affirms that the messengers did come, so one particle collapses the defense before argument can begin. Its compact, phonologically full answer licenses the next move, {{ar:فَ ٱدْعُوا۟}} ({{tr:fa idʿū}}), as consequence rather than counsel.

topics.headline: one-word reversal of denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the answer is confession because it reverses a negative question, not a simple yes.
topics.reason: The particle answers the preceding negative question and affirms the positive proposition.

topics.headline: admission pivots to command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the scene move from pleaded relief to interrogated admission and then to a dismissive command.
topics.reason: The answer particle stands alone as a complete quoted response and is followed by the consequential command sequence.

words.gloss_range: reported speech that restores the keepers' voice and introduces the directive dismissal
words.root_gloss_range: saying, uttering, declaring, and verbal direction; the local Form I perfect reports direct speech whose complement is an imperative

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: imperative command carried by this speech verb

words.prose: {{ar:قَالُوا۟}} ({{tr:qālū}}) restores the keepers' voice after the inmates' admission and makes saying itself deliver a command. The perfect reports a completed utterance, but its complement, {{ar:ٱدْعُوا۟}} ({{tr:idʿū}}), pushes the addressees into a futile test. This third speech frame turns the dialogue from concession into procedural dismissal.

topics.headline: saying becomes directive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices ordinary reported speech carrying the force of an authoritative dismissal.
topics.reason: The speech verb introduces a quoted imperative, and the plural subject marks the keepers' restored speaking role.

topics.headline: concession answered by command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the concession immediately answered by an order that exposes its futility.
topics.reason: The second and third saying clauses stand back-to-back, moving from answer to command.

words.gloss_range: consequential bound particle joining the admission to the command as an immediate result

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: imperative attached to the consequence particle

words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the command follow from the admission. The order is not helpful counsel after proof has been conceded; it is the procedural consequence of that concession. Because the particle is attached to {{ar:ٱدْعُوا۟}} ({{tr:idʿū}}), consequence and command arrive as one tight unit, pivoting from past notice to present recourse.

topics.headline: command follows from admission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command is procedurally compelled by the conceded proof.
topics.reason: The conjunction directly precedes the imperative and links it to the preceding answer.

topics.headline: proof turns into recourse test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the scene turn from acknowledged past warning to a present appeal whose futility will be stated.
topics.reason: The particle introduces the imperative response after the admission and before the verdict clause.

words.gloss_range: plural imperative to call or appeal, with its object left open so every recourse is exposed to the coming verdict
words.root_gloss_range: calling, summoning, invoking, appealing, and supplicating range; the local imperative selects commanded appeal with no expressed object

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the nominalized call judged in the closure

words.prose: {{ar:ٱدْعُوا۟}} ({{tr:idʿū}}) is a plural command with the object left unstated: call whomever you can. That openness lets the closing verdict cover every possible appeal, whether summons or supplication. The call requested from the keepers in 40:49 is returned to the inmates here with opposite authority. The same root then returns as {{ar:دُعَٰٓؤُا۟}} ({{tr:duʿāʾu}}), so the commanded action becomes the judged noun; what they are permitted to attempt is exactly what the ayah declares lost.

topics.headline: open appeal under command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command opens every possible direction of appeal before all appeal is judged futile.
topics.reason: The imperative is plural and has no expressed object, while the root range supports calling, summoning, and supplication in the local appeal frame.

topics.headline: requested call turned back on petitioners
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the call requested from the keepers in 40:49 returned to the inmates in 40:50 with opposite authority.
topics.reason: The concrete 40:49 to 40:50 comparison keeps the same call-root but reverses agency and authority.

topics.headline: command returns as judged noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the commanded action reappear as a nominal channel that the closure restricts to lostness.
topics.reason: The imperative and later verbal noun share the same local root and sit on either side of the verdict transition.

words.gloss_range: resumptive or adversative linker before negation, tying the command to its evaluative verdict

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: negative particle opening the verdict clause

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) prevents the command from floating as an open invitation. It ties the imperative directly to the negated verdict clause, so the closure can be heard as continuation, contrast, circumstance, and evaluation at once. With {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) following immediately, dialogue gives way to a general rule about the call's status.

topics.headline: command enveloped by verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command is immediately wrapped in its negative evaluation.
topics.reason: The conjunction stands before the negative nominal sentence that evaluates the command.

topics.headline: dialogue turns into general judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the exchange stop being back-and-forth dialogue and become a general verdict on the call.
topics.reason: The conjunction introduces the final negative nominal sentence rather than another quoted answer.

words.gloss_range: negative particle opening an exclusive nominal verdict that leaves one predicate-domain for the call

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: restriction particle completing the exclusive frame
the sole enclosing predicate-domain left by restriction

words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) opens the final exclusion. It negates the nominal sentence without needing a new action verb, so the call itself becomes the thing evaluated. Together with {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) and {{ar:فِى ضَلَٰلٍ}} ({{tr:fī ḍalālin}}), it makes the command's outcome predetermined: call, but the call has no effective domain except enclosing lostness.

topics.headline: negation opens exclusive verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees every effective value for the call excluded except being inside lostness.
topics.reason: The particle begins the negative nominal sentence completed by the later exception particle and prepositional predicate.

topics.headline: command judged without new event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closure denies efficacy categorically rather than narrating a failed attempt.
topics.reason: The final clause is nominal, with the verbal noun as subject and no new finite action verb.

words.gloss_range: verbal noun for calling or appeal, made the subject of the final restricted verdict and bound in construct to the rejecters
words.root_gloss_range: calling, summoning, invoking, appealing, and supplicating range; the local verbal noun abstracts the act into an evaluable subject

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the rejecters whose call is judged
preposition of containment in the final predicate
lostness as the predicate-domain containing the call

words.prose: {{ar:دُعَٰٓؤُا۟}} ({{tr:duʿāʾu}}) turns the commanded call into a noun that the sentence can judge. As the nominative subject of the nominal closure, it carries the verdict without a new event verb; the issue is the value of the calling-channel itself. Its construct with {{ar:ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ}} ({{tr:al-kāfirīna}}) keeps the failed appeal bound to its source, and the directed-call image remains sharp because that appeal is then trapped inside {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) {{ar:ضَلَٰلٍ}} ({{tr:ḍalālin}}).

topics.headline: call becomes judged subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the act of calling is frozen into a subject so its whole value can be judged.
topics.reason: The verbal noun is nominative subject in the final nominal sentence, with the prepositional phrase as predicate.

topics.headline: appeal bound to its source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the failed appeal classified by the people it belongs to, not by the one appealed to.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the following active participle as the construct complement of the verbal noun.

topics.headline: imperative echo becomes channel refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a specific petition answered by a universalizing verdict on the entire channel of calling.
topics.reason: The earlier imperative and this verbal noun share the root, and the final nominal construction evaluates the whole act.

words.gloss_range: definite active participle plural naming the rejecters as the source or possessors of the failed call
words.root_gloss_range: covering, concealing, denying, rejecting, ingratitude, and disbelief range; the local active participle selects settled rejecter identity after clear proof rather than agricultural, expiation, or place branches

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the clarity covered or rejected by this identity label

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ}} ({{tr:al-kāfirīna}}) is the construct complement of the call, so it marks whose appeal this is, not whom they call. The definite active participle names a settled class of rejecters, and after {{ar:ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ}} ({{tr:al-bayyināti}}) the covering pressure of the root becomes pointed: the proofs were not absent; clarity was covered over. The warning-admission parallel (67:9) sharpens this scene because admission here moves directly to futile appeal, and the shift from direct address to this third-person label strips the petitioners into the identity that owns the failed call.

topics.headline: appeal judged by its source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verdict concerns the call belonging to rejecters, not the identity of the one invoked.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the active participle the genitive construct complement of the verbal noun.

topics.headline: definite participle classifies them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a standing rejecter identity, not a single past act, owning the futile appeal.
topics.reason: The local form is a definite masculine plural active participle.

topics.headline: covered clarity explains the label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final rejecter label as covering admitted clarity, not ignorance without proof.
topics.reason: The local ayah has already named clear proofs and admission, so the covering or rejecting pressure remains locally anchored.

topics.headline: admission scene becomes identity label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a warning-admission scene like 67:9 sharpened here by moving directly to futile appeal and a third-person identity label.
topics.reason: The source rows give the concrete 67:9 comparison, while local grammar shifts from second-person interrogation to the third-person class label.

words.gloss_range: exception particle functioning with prior negation as restriction, leaving only the final prepositional domain

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: negative particle that begins the exclusive frame
preposition that opens the sole remaining frame
lostness as the sole remaining domain
the sole remaining frame after restriction

words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) completes the exclusion begun by {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}). It is not exempting a group; it restricts the predicate so that {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) {{ar:ضَلَٰلٍ}} ({{tr:ḍalālin}}) is the only possible frame left for the call. By delaying that sole remainder, the ayah makes lostness land as the terminal judgment and answers the earlier request for reduced punishment with total restriction of the calling itself.

topics.headline: only one predicate frame remains
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that no successful appeal is left outside the final lostness-domain.
topics.reason: The particle follows negation and precedes the sole remaining prepositional predicate.

topics.headline: lostness delayed as final remainder
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the sentence hold back its only remainder until lostness arrives as the final word-domain.
topics.reason: The restriction particle delays the predicate phrase that closes the ayah.

words.gloss_range: preposition forming the final predicate and locating the call inside a state or domain rather than directing it toward a destination

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: restriction particle before this final predicate phrase
the enclosing condition governed by the preposition

words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) forms the predicate that locates the call. The preposition does not say the call travels toward error; it says the call already exists within an enveloping condition. Because this predicate is delayed until after {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}), the verdict concentrates in the closing domain, {{ar:ضَلَٰلٍ}} ({{tr:ḍalālin}}).

topics.headline: call located inside lostness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices containment in a condition, not movement toward a destination.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the prepositional phrase the predicate of the call in the final nominal sentence.

topics.headline: predicate delayed to close verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the final judgment concentrated in the delayed prepositional phrase.
topics.reason: The predicate phrase appears after the restriction particle and closes with the final noun.

words.gloss_range: indefinite verbal noun naming an open-ended domain of error, lostness, wandering, and futile remedy as the final verdict
words.root_gloss_range: straying, losing the way, going wrong, being lost, misdirection, futility, and failed guidance range; the local verbal noun after the preposition selects an enclosing state-domain

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: clear proofs answered by final lostness
preposition that makes lostness an enclosing domain

words.prose: {{ar:ضَلَٰلٍ}} ({{tr:ḍalālin}}) is the final word and the sole domain left by restriction. Governed by {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}), it names not one mistake but an enclosing state of lostness, error, wandering, and futile remedy. The root image of losing the way remains vivid under containment: their call is not merely unanswered but situated in a pathless field after {{ar:ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ}} ({{tr:al-bayyināti}}) had already made things clear. The contrast with the prayer to avoid the straying ones (1:7) is negative and pointed: here the call remains inside lostness after proof.

topics.headline: lostness as the only remaining domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah landing on lostness as the domain that resolves the whole dialogue.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by the final preposition and supplies the only predicate-domain left by the restriction.

topics.headline: open-ended state of failed remedy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final state left qualitatively open: error, wandering, loss, and futility all remain in view.
topics.reason: The local noun is an indefinite verbal noun in the prepositional predicate.

topics.headline: rejected clarity ends in misdirection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees final lostness answer earlier clarity and turn the scene into a universalizing verdict.
topics.reason: The ayah begins the charge with clear proofs and ends the verdict with lostness.

topics.headline: negative echo of avoiding strayers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a negative contrast with 1:7: what is prayed to be avoided appears here as the domain containing the failed call.
topics.reason: The source rows give a concrete 1:7 contrast, and the local wording closes with the related lostness noun.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The three q-w-l turns at words 1, 7, and 9 frame the question, the admission bala, and the reply.
baseline_models.mechanism: A negotiated speech sequence converts carried, manifest evidence into the addressees' own concession; the final command follows a fact that their answer has put on record.

activation_trace.role: Mutual speaking and negotiation make the three turns a compact evidentiary colloquy.
The carrier and carried message supply the evidence-bearing party recalled by the question.
Manifest disclosure makes the admitted fact one of prior clarity, not unavailable notice.
Denial of disclosed truth names the issue that the answer bala can no longer contest.

changed_reading.before: The guards remind the addressees that messengers came, and the addressees agree.
changed_reading.after: The three-turn exchange converts once-denied clear evidence into the disbelievers' own on-record admission before their plea is dismissed.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The ayah opposes ta'tikum and rusulukum at words 4-5 to id'u and du'a at words 10 and 12, ending with fi dalal at word 16.
baseline_models.mechanism: Evidence has an inbound route and carrier that successfully reaches the addressees, whereas their outbound call is described through deviation and loss as lacking a viable return route.

activation_trace.role: Arrival and reaching establish the successful inbound movement of evidence.
A messenger carrying speech supplies the inbound channel and its bearer.
Calling by speech supplies the attempted outbound movement in both command and noun.
Deviation from guidance and intended course turns failed response into a routing failure.
Loss of an object sharpens the image of a call that cannot be located at its destination.

changed_reading.before: The disbelievers' prayer is simply ineffective.
changed_reading.after: The ayah draws a directional asymmetry: truth reached them by an arriving carrier, but their answering call now has no viable route to its intended destination.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Bayyinat at word 6, al-kafirin at word 13, and dalal at word 16 form a disclosure-covering-disappearance sequence.
baseline_models.mechanism: What was exposed and distinguishable is met by covering denial; the later call consequently enters hiddenness rather than producing a new disclosure.

activation_trace.role: Appearance and disclosure make the prior signs perceptibly open.
Covering supplies the material reversal applied to what had been made clear.
Hiddenness and disappearance provide the resulting state of the later call.
The voiced call is the item that passes from attempted expression into disappearance.

changed_reading.before: Their religious status explains why their supplication fails.
changed_reading.after: The status is rendered as an information sequence: what arrived exposed was covered over, so the later emitted call enters concealment rather than disclosure.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus question compresses a formula repeatedly enacted across the surah: messengers and clear proofs arrive, a resistant response follows, and the final dialogue reduces all former defenses to the single concession bala.

activation_trace.role: The three negotiated turns are the compressed replay's question-and-answer frame.
Manifest evidence is the focus anchor shared with the repeated chains.
The earlier arrival supplies the same successful approach expressed in the focus question.
The message carrier reproduces the focus ayah's named source of notice.
The same manifest-proof branch makes 40:22 a near-verbatim precursor.
Explicit denial supplies the omitted response that the focus's label al-kafirin recalls.
A second messenger occurrence near the close reopens the same carried-message sequence.
Repeated manifest proofs show that the focus question summarizes a surah-wide pattern.
Knowledge disclosed to its possessor supplies the competing store in which they rejoice instead of receiving the proofs.

structural_cues: 40:22 reproduces kana plus ta'ti plus rusul plus bayyinat and immediately adds fa-kafaru.
40:83 repeats rusul plus bayyinat near the surah's end, then places the recipients with the knowledge already in their possession.
The focus asks only whether the repeated chain occurred and receives an unqualified bala.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two close repetitions and their resistant responses; I infer that the focus question functions as a compressed replay or checksum of that history. A live alternative is that the repetition only reinforces notice without giving the dialogue a formal recap function.

changed_reading.before: The question recalls one past encounter with messengers.
changed_reading.after: The question is the terminal compression of a repeatedly narrated evidence-response chain, and bala collapses the surah's many defenses into self-confirmation.

context_deltas.mechanism: The condemned first try to transfer their petition to custodians; after settled judgment, the keepers return the act with fa-id'u. Earlier aligned protective petition and the explicit absence of an obeyed intercessor show that mediation is relational and procedural, not a technique available on demand.

activation_trace.role: Covering sin and protecting its bearer supplies an earlier other-directed petition aligned with faith and return.
An advocate joined to another supplies the explicitly unavailable proxy role for wrongdoers.
Judgment between people fixes the procedural state before the request to the keepers.
The keeper defined by custody, not advocacy, is the requested prayer proxy.
The inmates direct a spoken call-command to the custodians and ask them to relay it.
Lightening a burden specifies the narrowly delegated relief sought through the proxy.
The reply returns both the act and its failed result to the original petitioners.

structural_cues: 40:49 directly supplies the ellipsed request: the people in the fire ask the keepers to call their Lord for one day's reduction.
40:47-48 first shows followers seeking relief from former superiors, who answer that all are together under a judgment already made.
The pronoun movement from rabbakum in 40:49 to fa-id'u in 40:50 shifts agency from your Lord through us back to you.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a failed ladder from followers to leaders to keepers, plus earlier petition and unavailable intercession; I infer that fa-id'u rejects outsourced relation and reallocates agency. It may alternatively be only a dismissive imperative, without a general principle of non-transferability.

changed_reading.before: The guards tell the prisoners to pray for themselves because prayer will fail.
changed_reading.after: Custodians refuse to become advocacy proxies after judgment and return the call to those who had outsourced the relation they previously refused.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated d-a-w occurrences create a routing network: a call to faith is refused, calls beside God have no adjudicative power, reciprocal calls lead toward rescue or fire, God states an explicit call-response relation, and former invoked objects later disappear. The focus call fails within that inverted network rather than because calling is intrinsically futile.

activation_trace.role: The command and noun anchor the changed reading in the focus's attempted spoken call.
Loss supplies the focus endpoint against which the surah's other call routes are compared.
The earlier call bends speech toward faith and is met by covering denial.
Calling other addressees supplies the alternate outbound route.
Otherness marks the alternate route as directed beside the stated judge.
Decisive judgment contrasts God's adjudication with the invoked others' inability to adjudicate anything.
Reciprocal calls show that the same speech act can incline hearers toward opposed destinations.
Rescue by separation names one destination of the opposed invitations.
The called-toward object is stated to possess no effective call in either temporal domain.
The direct imperative to call supplies the positive side of the call relation.
Returning speech and answering explicitly completes the positive call-response circuit.
The speakers deny their former calling after its addressees are reported missing.
The vanished invoked objects literalize one pole of lostness while the repeated root extends disappearance into disorientation.

structural_cues: 40:12 and 40:14 contrast refusal when God alone is called with the command to call sincerely.
40:41-43 stages opposed invitations toward rescue and fire and then denies efficacy to the rival called-toward object.
40:60 states call Me and I answer you, preventing the focus from being read as a blanket denial of call-response.
40:74 joins former invocation, disappearance, denial of having invoked anything, and the same d-l-l root.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated d-a-w nodes, destinations, and one explicit answer; I infer a coherent routing network whose history determines the focus failure. A live alternative is that these are distinct uses of calling and only the immediate 40:49-50 exchange controls the focus.

changed_reading.before: The prayer is lost because no prayer from these speakers can work.
changed_reading.after: The prayer is the terminal output of an inverted call network: they refused the call that reached them, routed calls elsewhere, and now find the return channel they seek absent.

context_deltas.mechanism: Confession, decisive judgment, witness, and the non-benefit of excuse turn the focus exchange into post-judgment evidentiary closure. Bala is not new information for the guards; it is self-witness that removes the last factual premise for relief.

activation_trace.role: Negotiated speech anchors the judicially changed reading in the focus's three formal turns.
Manifest evidence supplies the proposition to which the speakers attest.
Confession as acknowledgment and submission supplies an earlier self-incriminating speech act tied to a request for exit.
Decisive judgment establishes the surah's contrast between true adjudication and powerless substitutes.
Judgment between the servants immediately precedes the appeal to the keepers.
Presence with witnessing supplies the public evidentiary setting named just after the focus.
Denied benefit makes the later excuse procedurally fruitless.
The excuse supplies the class of post-judgment speech into which the focus plea can now be heard.

structural_cues: 40:11 pairs confession of sins with a question about any route out.
40:47-50 moves through appeals to leaders, judgment already rendered, appeal to keepers, and the focus's factual question.
40:51-52 immediately names the standing of witnesses and the failure of wrongdoers' excuse to benefit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies legal and testimonial vocabulary around the dialogue; I infer that the guards ask for an admission that closes rather than investigates the record. The alternative is a rhetorical moral reminder with no procedural force.

changed_reading.before: Bala is a simple acknowledgment before an unanswered request.
changed_reading.after: Bala functions as self-witness after judgment, converting the plea into a non-beneficial excuse rather than reopening the merits.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah distinguishes a receptive interval, marked by forgiveness, acceptance, and return, from speech produced only after manifest evidence and then witnessed force. The focus call is therefore not merely at the wrong destination; it is made after its evidence-responsive window has closed.

activation_trace.role: Past occurrence and temporal presence place the messengers' arrival in an earlier phase.
Prior arrival marks the event to which a timely response could have attached.
The present call is the temporally displaced response contrasted with prior arrival.
Covering sin while protecting its bearer supplies the surah's open side of reception.
Acceptance with satisfaction establishes that return can be received rather than intrinsically rejected.
Habitual return supplies the responsive posture linked there to remembering the signs.
The carried message reappears at the late historical boundary before punishment is seen.
Manifest proof fixes the earlier disclosure to which the late speakers failed to respond.
Seeing with the eye marks the later phase in which declarative belief is finally voiced.
The explicit absence of benefit after sight supplies the temporal closure.
General loss names the settled result at the point where late belief no longer benefits.

structural_cues: 40:3 places forgiving and accepting return beside severe consequence and final destination.
40:83-85 orders clear-proof arrival, sight of force, a new declaration of belief, and an explicit statement that this late belief did not benefit.
The focus itself orders past messenger arrival before the present imperative to call.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies open reception language and an explicit late-belief non-benefit sequence; I infer a phase boundary between response to evidence and speech after witnessed consequence. The live alternative is that speaker identity alone, rather than timing, explains the focus's lost prayer.

changed_reading.before: The call misses because its route or addressee is wrong.
changed_reading.after: The call is also lost in time: correct-sounding speech after the evidentiary window cannot retroactively become the response that the arriving proofs required.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it hears prayer tactically rather than devotionally. It remains anchored because 40:25 and 40:50 use the same wa-ma X al-kafirin illa fi dalal frame, while 40:37 supplies a second failed-plot frame; render it as a syntactic and functional echo, not as lexical identity or a claim that prayer in general is plotting.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The nominal closure wa-ma du'a'u al-kafirina illa fi dalalin, anchored in d-a-w at words 10 and 12, k-f-r at word 13, and d-l-l at word 16.

activation_trace.role: Plotting and contrivance occupy the same grammatical slot later occupied by the focus prayer.
The identical disbeliever class binds the failed plot formula to the focus formula.
The identical exclusive endpoint in deviation supplies the strongest formal bridge.
A second contrivance enters the repeated wa-ma X illa fi Y failure mold.
Ruin and loss provide the alternate failed endpoint of the repeated plotting mold.
The focus substitutes voiced petition for plotting in the same failure-shaped frame.
The same denying agents preserve continuity across the tactical and devotional modes.
The repeated deviation endpoint makes the prayer look like the last maneuver in an unchanged trajectory.

changed_reading.before: A devotional plea receives no effective answer.
changed_reading.after: Within the surah's repeated failure formula, prayer becomes the disbelievers' final maneuver after coercive plots fail: the speech mode changes, but its trajectory does not.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is form-distant because it activates the packet's secondary d-a-a mapping for the focus d-a-w root. It remains anchored to the exact fa-id'u imperative and is reinforced by the keeper, dragging, and stoking sequence; render it only as a pragmatic and material undertone of rebuff, never as the lexical translation of id'u.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Fa-id'u at word 10, resolved through the packet's secondary mapped root root_000477 while retaining the source root d-a-w.

activation_trace.role: The keeper as custodian supplies the institutional voice from which the following pushback comes.
The inmates' literal call-command establishes what the keepers pragmatically throw back at them.
The secondary branch's violent push gives fa-id'u an exploratory undertone of custodial shove or rebuff.
Deviation supplies the direction into which the rebuffed action is sent.
A restraint fixed around the body materializes the custodial setting of constrained movement.
Dragging and extending continue the material motion suggested by the secondary push branch.
Stoking and intensifying fire supplies the destination of the carceral motion.

changed_reading.before: Fa-id'u is a neutral permission or command to attempt prayer.
changed_reading.after: As a contained secondary activation, fa-id'u carries custodial pushback: the requested proxy action is shoved back onto the prisoners and into the same carceral motion.

strongest_changes: The focus dialogue became a self-closing evidentiary recap of the messenger and clear-proof chain repeated at 40:22 and 40:83.
The lost prayer became a route-specific failure within a surah-wide network of refused calls, rival calls, explicit response, and vanished invoked objects.
The immediate 40:49 request made fa-id'u a refusal of delegated prayer after judgment rather than a general statement that prayer cannot be answered.
The 40:83-85 sequence made the prayer temporally lost: it is voiced after the evidence-responsive window has closed.
The exact 40:25 and 40:50 failure frames activated the contained reading of prayer as the disbelievers' last failed maneuver.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet did not merely add themes; it exposed repeated verbal circuits and exact syntactic molds. Most distinctive were the positive call-answer statement at 40:60 against the lost call at 40:50, the proxy ladder immediately before the focus, and the substitution of du'a for kayd inside an otherwise repeated failure formula.
remaining_uncertainties: Dalal may support a directional routing image more strongly than a literal non-arrival of speech.
The shared failure frame securely marks analogy, but the tactical reading of prayer should not erase the possibility of sincere late distress.
The secondary d-a-a activation is intentionally exploratory and may carry only pragmatic texture rather than interpretive weight.
The legal vocabulary supports evidentiary closure, but the exact procedural force assigned to bala remains reader inference.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Present unanswered calling is traced to rejected prior arrival.** `ء ت ي/B001` gives arriving messengers, `د ع و/B001` repeated calling, and `ض ل ل/B001` deviation from aim. The custodians make former evidence the reason no mediation now works. I infer that refusing an earlier communicative channel deforms the later one; prayer reads as directionless because its prior orientation was rejected.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The open divine invitation in 40:60 supplies the strongest contrast: calling itself is not futile; its direction and prior reception determine whether it reaches response.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **A once-open call route has become directionless.** Lexically, `د ع و:B001` is calling to draw near, while `ض ل ل:B001` is going astray from an aim and `B003` failing to locate something. Structurally, the keepers contrast messengers' earlier arrival with clear demonstrations to the prisoners' present call; the admission `بلى` leaves no evidentiary gap, yet the imperative `فادعوا` yields only loss. Call's role has reversed from offered approach to undeliverable plea. The packet gives the earlier message channel and current failed invocation; I infer that refusal of the former has destroyed the practical route expected in the latter. `في ضلال` thus describes a call unable to find its destination or effect.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 40:60 proves that calls are not inherently futile; the decisive difference is whether the caller accepted the open reciprocal relation before consequence closed the route.

inter_ayah_rows.note: It recounts former peoples receiving clear messengers, rejecting what they brought, and treating their call with doubt.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The caller's summons to a dreadful matter gives only a broad eschatological setting.

inter_ayah_rows.note: Messengers describe their call as forgiveness before an appointed term, making explicit the opportunity recalled too late in the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Following divine guidance removes fear, a faithful contrast to the fate implied in the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.note: Pharaoh's procedural response to Moses does not add to the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.note: Bringing truth to deniers offers a broad contrast but no new detail about their final plea.

inter_ayah_rows.note: The speakers confess after two deaths and two lives, then ask whether any exit remains; it is the same Fire dialogue immediately leading to the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The divine address recalls that they were called to faith but disbelieved, supplying the explicit prior refusal presupposed by the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Those in the Fire dispute their shared punishment, providing the larger dialogue sequence in which the focus's exchange occurs.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The leaders in the Fire deny they can relieve anyone's punishment and point to God's judgment, directly framing the prisoners' turn to the keepers in 40:49-50.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: God commands people to call on Him, while those too arrogant for worship enter Hell humbled; it sharply contrasts the proper call with the focus's belated one.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Those who deny the Book and what was sent with the messengers are singled out before their punishment, directly matching the focus's charge.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Chains and yokes being placed on the deniers develops the punitive outcome of rejecting messenger-borne revelation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Being dragged through boiling water and then burned in the Fire gives the concrete consequence surrounding the focus's futile plea.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Belief only after seeing punishment supplies a further instance of an irrevocably belated response.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Faith at the sight of divine severity is declared useless, clarifying why the focus's admission and prayer cannot avail.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The people of the Fire ask their Lord to bring them out and admit wrongdoing if they return; it is a particularly close parallel to the focus's lost request.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The command to remain in the Fire without speaking answers the kind of hopeless post-punishment plea represented in the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The inhabitants of the Blaze admit that listening or reasoning would have kept them from it, directly complementing the focus's reminder of rejected warnings.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The inhabitants of the Blaze confess their sin, a close parallel to the focus's admitted prior reception and rejection of clear messengers.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Mocking God's signs and being deceived by worldly life leads to no exit from the Fire and no opportunity to make amends, directly explaining the focus's finality.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The condemned call to the keeper of Hell for their Lord to end them, another direct example of a desperate but ungranted plea in the Fire.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: At judgment, humans and jinn are asked whether messengers came reciting signs and warning them; they testify against themselves, closely matching the focus's interrogation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The promise and warning given when messengers come reciting divine signs supplies the earlier opportunity against which the focus judges them.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Those who deny and arrogantly reject the signs are declared companions of the Fire, joining the focus's cause and setting.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: When their messengers come to take them, idolaters are asked about what they invoked besides God and testify to their own disbelief; it parallels final accountability.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Every community receives a messenger calling for worship of God and rejection of false objects, supplying the universal prior summons recalled in the focus.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Punishment does not come until a messenger has been sent, making explicit the justice underlying the focus's question.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The hypothetical plea that a messenger should have been sent before humiliation shows the very excuse that the focus declares unavailable.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The condemned are asked whether divine signs were recited to them and whether they denied them, closely paralleling the focus's retrospective question.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: People would otherwise plead that a messenger should have been sent before calamity; it reinforces the focus's answer that messengers did come.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: God does not destroy communities before sending a messenger to their center, supplying a justice principle behind the focus's rebuke.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: If the Messenger is denied, earlier messengers were also denied, adding the recurring pattern of rejecting the prophetic message.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Every community has had a warner, reinforcing the focus's premise that warning was already delivered.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The soul's regret for neglecting its duty to God gives a late-confession counterpart to the focus's irreversible setting.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The wish to return and do good after seeing punishment parallels the focus's failed attempt to respond only after the consequence arrives.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Whether the condemned endure or seek excuse, the Fire remains their abode and they are not restored to favor, sharpening the focus's hopelessness.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The guilty remain permanently in the punishment, giving the enduring finality behind the focus's command to pray without relief.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu dalı sesle ortaya çıkarılan söz ve harflerden kurulu sözlü ifade olarak verir. Geçici çerçeve aynı çekirdeği taşıyor; dil organı, hükümdar unvanı ve mecazi yan kullanımlar bu dalın dışında kalır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal çıplak söz söyleme ve söylenmiş söz çekirdeğidir; organ, unvan, söylenti ve mecazlar ayrı dallardır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam bare olduğu için tanım çıplak söyleme ve sözlü ifade anlamıyla sınırlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir düşünceyi veya sözü sesli biçimde dışa vurma ve böyle dışa vurulmuş harfli sözlü ifade anlamıdır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek işlem, sözü sesli olarak dışa çıkarmaktır.
Söylenen şey tek söz, cümle, şiir veya konuşma ölçeğinde olabilir.
Ad biçimleri aynı söylenmiş söz alanında toplanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, sözü sesle dışa çıkarılan ve harflerden oluşan sözlü ifade çekirdeğinde toplar; ad biçimleri de aynı alana bağlıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Sözü sesli biçimde ortaya koyma ve ortaya konmuş sözlü ifade için genel başlık olarak uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Sesle dışa vurma ve sözlü ifade çekirdeğini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Fiil bağlamında kişinin sözü sesli olarak ortaya koymasını karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Fiilsel söyleme işlemini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Ad bağlamında söylenmiş söz veya konuşma ürünü için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Söylenmiş ifade sonucunu korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal sözün sesle dışa vurulmasını ve söylenmiş ifadeyi anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal konuşmayı sağlayan organ olan dili adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İkisi de konuşma alanına bağlıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Okur karışıklığı söz ile onu üreten organ arasındadır. Bu dalda ürün ve eylem merkezdir; komşuda bedensel araç merkezdir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal hem söyleme eylemini hem de söylenmiş söz adlarını kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal konuşmanın dille çıkarılıp lafza dönüşmesi üzerinde durur.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İkisi de sözün sesli hale gelmesini paylaşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu daha doğrudan telaffuz olayına odaklanır; bu dalda söylenmiş sözün ad alanı da çekirdeğe dahildir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal bir sözün söylenmesini veya söylenmiş olmasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal sözün insanlar arasında yayılıp söylentiye dönüşmesini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her ikisinde de söylenen söz bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dalda yayılma şart değildir; komşu dalda sözün dolaşıma girmesi anlamın asli sınırıdır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Aday komşular konuşma, dil, fasıhlık, unvan ve yan kullanımlar alanından tarandı; yayımlanan ayrımlar en yakın sınır karışıklıklarını verir.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه قال يقول قولا، والقول والقيل، والكلام المركب من الحروف إذا أبرز بالنطق، مفردا كان أو جملة أو قصيدة أو خطبة.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه اللسان نفسه، ولا لقب القيل الحميري، ولا الدلالة غير اللفظية إلا في فروعها الخاصة.
branches.source_phrase_ar: القول من النطق (maqayis)؛ قال يقول قولا وقولة ومقالا ومقالة (sihah)؛ القول والقيل واحد (mufradat)؛ المركب من الحروف المبرز بالنطق (mufradat)؛ القيل من القول اسم (ayn)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi ilgili biçimi doğrudan konuşma organı olan dil diye açıklar. Geçici çerçeve bu organ anlamını doğru taşır ve söylenmiş söz ya da söz sahibi anlamlarını bu dalın dışında bırakır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal organ adıdır; sözün kendisini, konuşma eylemini veya unvan sahibini kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam bare olduğu için tanım, tek biçimin çıplak organ anlamına bağlı kalır.

concept_map.definition: Söz söylemeye araç olan konuşma organı, yani dil anlamıdır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek anlam, konuşmayı sağlayan bedensel organdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar bu dalı konuşma organı olan dil anlamında ortaklaştırır; söz veya unvan anlamı eklenmez.

concept_gloss.applicability: Sözün kendisi değil, sözü çıkaran bedensel araç kastedildiğinde uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Organ anlamını ve konuşma işlevini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Organ adı olarak doğal çeviridir; bağlam konuşma eylemini değil organı göstermelidir.

error_profile.preserves: Türkçedeki organ adını korur.
error_profile.adds: Türkçede aynı kelime konuşulan sistem anlamını da çağırabilir.
error_profile.collision: Dil kelimesi dil sistemiyle karışabilir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal konuşmanın organını adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal sözü söyleme eylemini ve söylenmiş ifadeyi anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İkisi de konuşma ve söz alanında bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal araçtır; komşu dal bu araçla çıkan söz veya söyleme işlemidir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal tek özel biçimin söz organı anlamını verir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal organın genel adı, gücü, cinsiyeti ve çoğulları gibi daha geniş ad alanını taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İkisi de bedensel konuşma organını paylaşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Anlam merkezleri örtüşür; komşu dal organ adının daha geniş sözlük ailesini kapsadığı için sınır tam değildir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal konuşma organının kendisini belirtir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal konuşamama veya konuşmanın tutulması durumunu belirtir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İkisi de konuşma yetisiyle ilgilidir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Organ adı ile konuşma yokluğu aynı alanı paylaşır, fakat birinin çekirdeği araç, diğerinin çekirdeği yoksunluktur.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Aday komşular organ, konuşma bozukluğu, ses ve ana kök dalları açısından değerlendirildi; en doğrudan organ-karşıtlıkları yayımlandı.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه المقول بمعنى اللسان.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه القول المنطوق نفسه ولا صاحب القول.
branches.source_phrase_ar: المقول اللسان (maqayis;ayn;sihah)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kişiyi çok sözlü, güzel konuşan veya dili güçlü biri olarak niteleyen adları bir araya getirir. Bu, bir kez söyleme eylemi değil, kişide yerleşik konuşkanlık veya söz becerisi niteliğidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal kişi niteliğidir; tekil söyleme eylemi veya insanlar arasında yayılan söylenti değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam non_bare olduğu için tanım, kişi niteleyen özel biçimlerle sınırlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişiyi çok konuşan, dili güçlü veya söz söylemede atak olarak niteleyen kullanımdır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek anlam, kişide söz söyleme çokluğu veya söz becerisi niteliğidir.
Nitelik özellikle insan için kullanılır ve tek bir söyleme olayını göstermez.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar bu dalı kişiyi çok sözlü, dili güçlü veya konuşkan diye niteleyen biçimler etrafında ortaklaştırır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir kişinin konuşkanlığı veya söz söyleme gücü nitelendiğinde uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Kişi niteliğini ve söz çokluğunu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kişi hakkında çok söz söyleme niteliği vurgulandığında doğal çeviridir.

error_profile.preserves: Söz çokluğu niteliğini korur.
error_profile.loses: Dilin güçlü veya etkili oluşu ayrıca söylenmeyebilir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Söz becerisi ve etkili konuşma yönü öne çıktığında uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Söz söyleme gücü niteliğini korur.
error_profile.loses: Sadece konuşma çokluğu yönünü ikinci plana iter.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal kişinin yerleşik konuşkanlık veya söz becerisi niteliğidir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal söyleme eylemi ve söylenmiş sözün kendisidir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İkisi de söz söyleme alanından gelir.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İkisi de insanın dil ve söz gücü niteliğidir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Yakınlık konuşma gücündedir; komşuda sertlik ve olumsuz ton belirginleşirken bu dalda çok söz söyleme çekirdeği daha geniştir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal genel konuşkan veya dili güçlü kişi niteliğidir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal özellikle hitabeti güçlü kişiyi belirtir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İkisi de söz söyleme becerisine bağlı kişi niteliğidir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu daha mesleki veya gösterişli hitabete yaklaşır; bu dal sıradan çok sözlülüğü de içerir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Aday komşular konuşma becerisi, fasıhlık, sert dil ve kişi niteliği açısından tarandı; en yakın kişi nitelemeleri seçildi.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه قولة وقوال وقوالة وتقوالة وقؤول ومقوال ومقول إذا وصفت الإنسان بأنه لسن أو كثير القول أو منطيق.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه مجرد وقوع فعل قال مرة واحدة، ولا القالة الفاشية بين الناس.
branches.source_phrase_ar: رجل قولة وقوال كثير القول (maqayis)؛ رجل تقوالة أي منطيق وقوال وقوالة أي كثير القول (ayn)؛ رجل مقول ومقوال وقولة وقوال وتقوالة أي لسن كثير القول (sihah)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi belirli bir eski bölgesel yönetici unvanını, çoğullarını, kadın biçimini ve sözü geçerli kişi açıklamasını birlikte verir. Geçici çerçeve, sıradan söz anlamı değil unvan ve otorite anlamı olduğunu doğru sınırlar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal unvan ve makam sahibidir; sıradan söylenmiş söz veya söylenti anlamı değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam bare olduğu için tanım bu adların çıplak unvan anlamını verir.

concept_map.definition: Sözü geçerli kabul edilen yerel hükümdar veya yönetici unvanı, onun çoğulları ve kadın için kullanılan biçimi anlamıdır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek anlam, sözü geçen yönetici veya hükümdar unvanıdır.
Dal çoğul adları ve kadın için kullanılan unvan biçimini de içerir.
Unvanın açıklaması, sözü yürüyen kişi fikrine bağlanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Aktarım, bölgesel bir yönetici unvanını ve çoğullarını sözü geçerli kişi açıklamasıyla birleştirir; sıradan söz anlamından ayrıdır.

error_profile.preserves: Yönetici ve otorite anlamını korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi azlığı çokluğun karşıtı olarak verir; ayrıca yoksulluk, düşüklük, bir şeyi az görme ve belirli yapılarda yokluğa ya da seyrekliğe yaklaşan kullanımları açıkça destekler.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin sayı, miktar ya da ölçü bakımından çok olmayışını bildirir. Bundan yoksulluk ve düşüklük, bir şeyi az sayma veya az gösterme ve belirli yapılarda hiçlik ya da seyrek gerçekleşme anlamları gelişir.

facets.statement: Bir varlığın sayı, miktar veya ölçü bakımından çok olmayışıdır.
Azlık, kişinin yoksullaşması veya toplum içinde düşük ve değersiz görülmesi sonucuna uzanabilir.
Bir şeyi gerçekte ya da değerlendiren kişinin gözünde az sayma ve az gösterme anlamını taşır.
Belirli olumsuzluk ve sıklık yapılarında hiç yokluğu veya bir eylemin pek seyrek gerçekleşmesini anlatır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar azlığın temel sayı ve miktar karşıtlığında birleşir; yoksulluk ve düşüklük, az sayma ve bazı yapılarda yokluğa yaklaşan kullanım bu çekirdeğin düzenli uzantılarıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyin en üstünü veya başını çekirdek anlam olarak verir; dağın yuvarlak üst bölümü, insan başı ve kılıcın başındaki topuz bu çekirdeğin açık uzmanlaşmalarıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel baş ve en üst bölüm anlamı ile dağ tepesi, insan başı ve kılıç topuzu gibi yapıya bağlı uzmanlaşmalar ayrı tutulur.

facets.statement: Küpe benzeyen, özellikle sıvı taşımaya veya saklamaya elverişli büyük bir kaptır.
Belirli bir bölgeyle anılan iri küpler veya büyük toprak kaplar bu adın tanınmış bir türünü oluşturur.
İki büyük kap, bu iki kabın kendisini veya onların aldığı sıvı miktarını bildiren bir ölçü değeri kazanır.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol iri küpün yanı sıra küpün yerleştirildiği tahta destekleri de kapsayabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki kol da çok büyük bir küpü veya fıçımsı saklama kabını adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Kap nesnesinde güçlü bir örtüşme vardır; bu kol ölçü değerine uzanırken komşu kol kabın yerleştirildiği desteği de kapsayan farklı bir sınır kurar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol kabın özellikle iri oluşunu ve iki kaplık ölçü değerini belirtir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol genel bir küp veya saklama kabını büyüklük koşulu olmadan adlandırabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki kol da küp biçimindeki büyükçe saklama kapları için kullanılabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu kolda büyük kapasite kurucu bir özelliktir; komşu kartta kap türü öndedir ve aynı ölçü uzantısı bulunmaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol büyük bir küpü ve ona dayalı kapasite ölçüsünü bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol bir şeyin başını, tepesini veya en üst bölümünü bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Aynı kökün sesçe yakın iki ayrı anlam kolu olmaları dışında ortak çekirdekleri yoktur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Biri hacimli bir kap ve onun ölçüsüdür; diğeri bir varlığın uzamsal olarak en üstteki parçasıdır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; büyük küp anlamına en yakın iki kap komşusu ile aynı kökteki tepe anlamından ayrım, sınırı göstermek için yeterli ve yinelenmeyen karşılaştırmalardır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yükü taşıma veya taşıyabilme ile öznenin yükselip harekete geçmesini aynı kolda açıkça toplar; kuşun uçuşa kalkması, göğün yükselmesi ve yolcuların yüklenip ayrılması ayrı katılımcı gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Taşıma, yükselme ve yüklenerek yola koyulma bu kolun sınırıdır; salt sayısal azlık bu anlamlara katılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yük taşıma ile yükselme çekirdek çizgileri ayrılır; ağır bulut taşıma, uçuşa kalkma ve yolcuların ayrılması yalnızca kendi özne ve yapılarında geçerlidir.

concept_map.definition: Bir yükü kaldırıp taşıyabilmeyi veya üstlenmeyi ve bir öznenin yükselerek harekete geçmesini bildirir. İkinci çizgi kuşun uçuşa kalkmasını, göğün yükselmesini ve yolcuların yüklenip yola koyulmasını kapsar.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi kaldıracak gücü bulmak, onu taşımak veya yük olarak üstlenmektir.
Bir öznenin aşağıdaki konumundan yükselmesi veya kuş gibi harekete ve uçuşa başlamasıdır.
Yolcuların yüklerini alıp bulundukları yerden ayrılarak yolculuğa başlamasıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar bir yükü kaldırıp taşıma ile yukarı kalkarak harekete geçme çizgilerini bir araya getirir; kuş, gök, bulut ve yolcu örnekleri katılımcıya göre bu iki çizgiyi somutlaştırır.

concept_gloss.text: yük kaldırma, yükselme ve yola koyulma
concept_gloss.applicability: Taşıma, yukarı kalkma ve yüklenerek hareket etme çizgilerinin birlikte özetlenmesi gereken kavram haritasında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yük üstlenme, yükselme ve yolculuk için harekete geçme bileşenlerini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin veya başka bir taşıyıcının bir nesnenin ağırlığını üstlenmesi bağlamında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yükü kaldırma gücü ile onu fiilen taşıma anlamlarını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Göğün yükselmesi veya kuşun uçuşa kalkması gibi yukarı yönlü hareket bağlamlarında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yukarı kalkma ile uçuş için yerden ayrılma değerlerini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir topluluğun yolculuk yüklerini alarak bulunduğu yerden ayrılması bağlamına özgüdür.

error_profile.preserves: Yük alma, ayrılma ve yolculuğa başlama aşamalarını birlikte korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol yükü taşımanın yanında yükselme, havalanma ve yüklenerek ayrılma anlamlarını da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol yükü taşıma eyleminden çok onu taşıyacak güce sahip olmayı öne çıkarır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki kol da bir yükün ağırlığını karşılayacak gücü ve taşıma yeterliğini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Taşıma yeterliği ortak olsa da bu kol fiilî taşıma ve yerden yükselme yönlerine açılır; komşu kol güç yetirme sınırında kalır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol yük üstlenmeyi, kuşun havalanmasını ve yolcuların yüklenerek ayrılmasını kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol kişinin oturduğu yerden kalkmasını ve bir nesneyi bulunduğu yerden kaldırmayı kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki kol da aşağıdaki veya durağan bir konumdan kalkma ve hareket başlangıcını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu kol yükselmeyi taşıma ve yolculukla bağlar; komşu kol bedensel olarak ayağa kalkma ve nesneyi yerinden kaldırma çevresindedir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kolda yolculuk anlamı yolcuların yüklerini alıp bulundukları yerden ayrılmasıyla sınırlıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol yol üzerinde ilerlemeyi ve belirli bir hedefe doğru seyahat etmeyi genel olarak bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki kol da bir yerden ayrılarak yolculuğa başlama durumunda buluşur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu kol başlangıçtaki yüklenme ve kalkış anını anlatır; komşu kol yolculuğun kendisini ve hedefe doğru ilerlemeyi çekirdek edinir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar karşılaştırıldı; taşıma gücü, yerden kalkma ve yolculuğa başlama komşuları bu kolun üç kurucu yönünü en az yinelemeyle açıklar.

branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس مجرد القلة العددية، ولا قلة الجبل، ولا الرعدة
branches.source_phrase_ar: أقل الجرة أطاق حملها؛ استقلت السماء ارتفعت؛ استقل القوم مضوا وارتحلوا (sihah)؛ أقل الرجل الشيء واستقله إذا احتمله؛ استقل الطائر إذا نهض للطيران؛ استقل النبات أناف؛ استقل القوم إذا احتملوا ظاعنين؛ أقلت سحابا ثقالا أي حملت؛ قل إذا رفع وقل إذا علا (tahdhib)؛ أقلت سحابا ثقالا أي احتملته؛ أقللت كذا وجدته قليل المحمل (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kişiyi korku veya öfke yüzünden tutan titreme ve silkinişi açıkça tanımlar; genel hareket kararsızlığı değil, duygusal tetikleyicisi bulunan bedensel bir sarsıntı söz konusudur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol insanda korku veya öfkeyle beliren titremeyle sınırlıdır; nesnelerin genel sallanma ve yerinde duramama hali ayrı koldadır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Duygudan doğan titreme temel addır; kişiyi titremenin tutması ve öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi yalnızca ilgili yapılara bağlı anlatımlardır.

concept_map.definition: Bir insanın korku veya öfke yüzünden titremesi, ürpermesi ya da bedensel olarak silkelenmesidir. Durum, kişiyi bir titreme nöbetinin tutması veya öfkenin titremeyle dışa vurulması biçiminde anlatılabilir.

facets.statement: İnsan bedeninde beliren titreme, ürperti veya istemsiz silkiniş halidir.
Titremenin belirleyici nedeni korku ya da öfkedir.
Belirli yapılarda titremenin kişiyi tutması veya kişinin öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi anlatılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar insandaki titreme ve silkinişte birleşir; korku ile öfke başlıca nedenlerdir ve durum hem kişiyi tutan bir nöbet hem öfkenin bedensel belirtisi olarak anlatılır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Duygusal nedeni ve bedensel titremeyi birlikte taşıyan bütün kol için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Korku veya öfke koşulunu ve bunun doğurduğu bedensel titremeyi birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Korkunun yol açtığı kısa ve istemsiz bedensel titreme bağlamında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Korkuya bağlı istemsiz titreme ve silkiniş hissini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Titremenin kişiyi birden tutan belirgin bir durum olarak anlatıldığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Titremenin kişiyi tutan bedensel bir olay olarak sunuluşunu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Öfkenin bedensel titreme halinde dışa vurulduğu kişi bağlamlarına özgüdür.

error_profile.preserves: Öfke nedenini ve onunla birlikte ortaya çıkan titremeyi korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol titremenin korku veya öfkeden doğmasını anlam sınırının parçası yapar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol insandaki titreme veya silkinişi belirli bir duygusal nedenle sınırlamaz.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki kol da insan bedeninde ortaya çıkan titreme veya silkinişi adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bedensel olay aynıdır; bu kol korku ve öfke koşulunu taşırken komşu kart neden bakımından daha genel kalır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol korkunun yanında öfkeyi de titremenin belirleyici nedeni olarak içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol hastalık, gevşeklik, yumuşaklık ve korkaklıkla ilişkili titremeleri de kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki kol da özellikle korku sırasında insanda görülen titreme ve ürpermede örtüşür.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Korkuya bağlı kullanımda yakınlaşırlar; bu kol öfkeyi ekler, komşu kol ise hastalık ve bedensel gevşeklik gibi başka nedenlere açılır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar incelendi; genel insan titremesi ve nedenleri daha geniş ürperme alanı, bu kolun kişi ve duygu sınırını en iyi gösterir.
